questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Malawi?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter L and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: The capital of Malawi is Lilongwe and the spoken languages are English and Chichewa.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Malawi?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter M and has 10 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: It has borders with the countries of Tanzania, Zambia, and Mozambique.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “By 1500 AD groups came together and made Maravi empire, which streched from north of what is now Nkhotakota to the Zambezi River and from Lake Malawi to the Luangwa River in what is now _____.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter Z and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: By 1500 AD groups came together and made Maravi empire, which streched from north of what is now Nkhotakota to the Zambezi River and from Lake Malawi to the Luangwa River in what is now Zambia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Under pressure for free politics, Banda held an referendum in _____, where population voted for many party, democratic government.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 90s of the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: Under pressure for free politics, Banda held an referendum in 1993, where population voted for many party, democratic government.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Federation ended in _____ and the protection of the United Kingdom over Nyasaland ended in 1964.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 60s of the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malawi article.

questions.proof: The Federation ended in 1963 and the protection of the United Kingdom over Nyasaland ended in 1964.
